nodes.title: Any picture - swap it between runs
Note
widgets_values:
# TEST: EPS Image Grid - a pile of pictures that survives between runs

**Just press Run.** No checkpoint, no lora, no GPU, no setup - it loads one
image, drops a copy in the grid's buffer, and saves it. Takes a second.

The point of this node: normally a workflow only knows about the picture you
hand it *this* run. The Image Grid remembers every picture you have fed it,
run after run, and can hand the whole pile back later. The buffer lives on
disk, so quitting ComfyUI does not lose it.

## Pass 1 - collect three (about thirty seconds)

The node ships in **Collect** mode. Press **Run**. Then pick a different
picture in the Load Image node and Run again. Then a third. Three runs.

- Three thumbnails appear on the node.
- Three files in `output/eps_gridtest/`.

One picture in, one picture out, every time. Collect passes **only the
picture you just fed in** downstream - the buffer is a side effect, not the
output.

## Pass 2 - flip to Emit (the real trick)

Change **mode** to **Emit** and press Run **once**.

You get **four** files this time, not one. Emit sends the whole buffer
downstream in the order you collected it, and adds whatever is wired in
right now on the end. Three collected + one wired = four, out of one Run.

That is the whole feature: gather things over a morning, fan them all out in
one go.

## Pass 3 - restart and prove it stuck

Quit ComfyUI. Start it again. Load this workflow, leave it on **Emit**, Run.
Still four files. The buffer is not stored in the workflow - it is on disk,
tied to this node.

## Pass 4 - clear it

Press **Clear** on the node. Thumbnails go, buffer goes, and an Emit run now
passes through only the one wired picture again.

## Worth knowing

- **Add images...** and **Add folder...** on the node load straight into the
  buffer without running anything. Handy for pointing it at a folder of
  references you already have.
- The node ships with an **empty** id on purpose. The first time it loads it
  makes its own. That is why two copies of this workflow do not end up
  fighting over one buffer - and why you should never type an id in by hand.
- There is no size cap on the buffer. It is your disk, so keep half an eye on
  it if you are collecting big pictures.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
## Collect vs Emit

**Collect** - this run's picture goes downstream, *and* into the pile.

**Emit** - the whole pile goes downstream, this run's picture last.

Everything else on the node is buffer housekeeping: the thumbnails, **Clear**,
and the two bulk **Add** buttons. Click a thumbnail to see it big; a
thumbnail has its own little remove button.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values:
## Count the files, not the thumbnails

You get `eps_gridtest/frame_00001_.png`, `_00002_`, and so on.

In **Collect** mode that is one new file per Run.

In **Emit** mode it is one file per buffered picture, plus one for whatever
is wired in. Same graph, same Run button - the mode is the only thing that
changed.
